perspective:
From Maria Ortega’s perspective:

- I noticed Cheryl at the community center looking stressed and overwhelmed by the paperwork and planning for a new outreach project.
- I offered to help her; Cheryl accepted and said she could really use the help.
- After helping Cheryl, I observed that she was handling responsibilities better and growing more confident.
- At a staff meeting, I suggested Cheryl for a leadership role, praising her aptitude and commitment. The team leader supported the idea and asked Cheryl; Cheryl thanked me and said she was ready to take on the challenge.
- I later worried that Cheryl might feel I overstepped by suggesting her for leadership, so I privately approached her to make sure she felt supported, not pressured.
- Cheryl told me she was a bit surprised but appreciated my support and that my belief in her meant a lot.
- After that conversation, I felt relieved. I then proposed that we co-lead the project together.
- Cheryl agreed enthusiastically, saying my guidance had been invaluable and that we make a great team.
- Since then, we have successfully collaborated on several projects. I told Cheryl our collaboration had been fruitful and asked if she wanted to team up for more projects. Cheryl said she would love that and expressed excitement about what we can achieve together.
